entities.name: Quintus Fabius Maximus Gurges
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Quintus Fabius Q. f. M. n. Maximus Gurges was a Roman consul in 292, 276, and 265 BC, salvaging his reputation after a dissolute youth and a significant military defeat during his first consulate. He became a successful general, eventually holding the highest honours of the Roman state, but was slain in battle during his third and final consulate.

Gurges was the son of Quintus Fabius Maximus Rullianus, a renowned Roman general in his own right, and his early life was marked by a tumultuous relationship with his father. Despite this, Gurges proved himself to be a capable leader, playing a key role in several battles, including the Battle of Agrigentum in 264 BC, where he was fatally wounded.

Gurges' legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he played a significant role in shaping Roman politics and society during the 3rd century BC. His influence can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Scipio family, who would go on to dominate Roman politics for decades.

The Roman historian Livy would later describe Gurges as a 'most excellent general', highlighting his military prowess and strategic brilliance.

In the annals of Roman history, Quintus Fabius Q. f. M. n. Maximus Gurges stands as a testament to the enduring power of family, legacy, and military excellence.
